title: The Patient Harvest
premise: Zephyrine Almeida has spent her career listening to the dying count backwards, a private liturgy she records in her hospice notebooks. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the town's oldest well, the counting spreads to the living — and Zephyrine realizes the numbers are not prayers but a harvest schedule, and the door is a mouth. To save the ragtag family she has built from patients and coworkers, she must lead them out ahead of the final count before the well refills and takes its tithe; in the end she trades her own name into the ledger so the others can cross the threshold, becoming the last voice the door hears before it seals itself again.
about_author: Noor Oyelaran is a former palliative care volunteer who writes horror about tenderness under pressure. She lives near a river with too many old wells and insists this is unrelated.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Last Breath
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. In her hospice ward, Zephyrine documents Mr. Okonkwo's backwards count to zero, then finds the same numbers scrawled on his window from outside. A news report mentions the excavation crew striking a sealed door beneath the old well. Emotional beat: quiet dread — her sacred ritual of documentation becomes evidence that something is answering back.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: POV: rotating between Zephyrine and her found family — night aide Tomas, retired patient Marisol, teenage volunteer Dev. The counting begins among the living; Marisol counts down days instead of breaths. The crew opens the door and finds scratch marks on the inside, facing out. Emotional beat: belonging tested as fear makes them cling tighter while the town pulls apart.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. The well floods upward without rain, and those who reach zero walk toward it smiling. Zephyrine decodes her notebooks: the counts are a ledger, and names entered can be traded out. She plans the exodus through the door's far side, but Dev's countdown hits single digits. Emotional beat: desperate clarity — love expressed as logistics, prayer as paperwork.

chapters.title: What the Door Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine, closing on Tomas's epilogue. She leads her family across the threshold as the well refills, entering her own name into the ledger to balance theirs. The door seals from the inside around her; the counting stops everywhere at once. Weeks later, Tomas finds her final notebook page: not a count, just their names, kept safe. Emotional beat: grief braided with grace — found family endures because someone stayed behind to hold it.
